Fries, I got an electric fryer. I used to use cast iron, but it's just too much of a hassle.

Anyway, for the perfect French fries, cut your potatoes, and immediately put them in water. I usually drain the bowl and refill it. Let it sit for 50 mins to an hour, and then strain the water, let them dry the best you can.

Tallow and duck fat. Heat it to 325° Freedom, and drop the fries in for 4-5 minutes. Remove them from the oil, and if you are making multiple batches, set these aside carefully, they will be soft and easily damaged. After all the fries have had the initial dip, heat up the oil to 400° Freedom. Put the half cooked fries back in, and be careful because at that temp it will be bubbling high (another reason I switched to a fryer). Let them cook until golden brown, ~8 minutes. Pull one out, salt it, let it rest a minute, and judge from there if they need to cook longer. Also note, they're crispier when they first come out, so if you think the one you just tried was perfect, let them cook maybe a minute longer.

If you're doing multiple batches, have the oven set to 200, and have the finished batch hang out in there while you are frying the next batch.

Rabbits are often known affectionately by the pet name "bunny" or "bunny rabbit," especially when referring to young, domesticated rabbits. Originally, the word for an adult rabbit was "coney" or "cony," while "rabbit" referred to the young animals. More recently, the term "kit" or "kitten" has been used to refer to a young rabbit. A group of young rabbits is referred to as a "kindle." Young hares are called "leverets," and this term is sometimes informally applied to any young rabbit. Male adult rabbits are called "bucks" and female adult rabbits are known as "does." A group of rabbits or hares is often called a "fluffle" in parts of Northern Canada. A group of rabbits is called a "herd."
